summary: Introductory sync between setter Kim Forbes-Sobers (KFS) and newly onboarded closer Richard Claessen. They debrief Richard's first sets — a prospect named Teresa/Teresita who took the call from a restaurant while eating and was rebooked, and a cancelled set (John) with a bad phone number. They agree on set-note preferences: flag talkers, give a one-line goal, no detailed discovery notes. Kim confirms the KFS suffix convention marks his sets. The rest is background: Kim is 21, seven months in the role, ex door-to-door and solar sales, recruited off a Trevor Instagram post; Richard is 20, Dutch, based in Bulgaria, roughly a year closing, came in via Chris Klevan after a failed stint on a real estate offer. They close on how price lands with European vs American prospects.
notable: Richard states his intent to close a prospect at the lowest possible number, '$200 a month', to secure his first close on the offer — far below the $6,000/6mo and $9,000/12mo offer.

Richard describes deliberately quoting European prospects in euros/pounds rather than USD because the converted figure sounds smaller: 'of course they don't know it's originally 6k, but just 4k, 4.5k sounds a lot cheaper than 6k.'
Both men disparage a live prospect's body and eating on the recording ('she's big and then eating noodles', 'whoa, she's big'), and Richard directs Kim to watch the call recording for it.
Setter code confirmed from the source: 'if I set somebody, I add KFS to the end of their thing' — Kim Forbes-Sobers = KFS.

Kim describes the pre-Chris Klevan process as price-transparent at set stage ('everyone that shows already knows the price') and the current process as deliberately withholding price until the closer sells it, which raised show-stage qualification but was changed to capture people who would not take the call knowing the price.
Kim states set volume is roughly 25 sets a week over the past three months, currently down due to an advertising change.
Richard notes he does not train with kettlebells yet and plans to add them so he can tell prospects he uses them himself.
Richard characterises American prospects as higher no-show but easier to close, Europeans as harder to close and more data-driven — a heuristic being applied to live sets.
